initiatives.name: Portfolio Simplification & Focus on Energy
initiatives.summary: DCC is simplifying its portfolio to focus solely on energy, divesting Healthcare and Technology businesses, and will change its name to DCC Energy plc. This represents a fundamental business model shift from a diversified conglomerate to a single-sector energy company.

evidence.title: Portfolio simplification reducing complexity and refocusing on energy
evidence.summary: DCC executed a significant portfolio simplification by selling DCC Healthcare and exiting DCC Technology's Info Tech business, materially reducing operational complexity, working capital volatility and capital intensity to concentrate capital and management attention on energy.
evidence.quote: During the period, we completed the sale of DCC Healthcare, exited DCC Technology’s Info Tech business, and returned significant capital to our shareholders. These steps have materially changed the structure of the Group and reduced operational complexity, working capital volatility and capital intensity.

evidence.title: Significant headcount reduction from 16,777 to 11,700 FTEs
evidence.summary: Total FTEs decreased from 16,777 to 11,700, largely due to the divestments of DCC Healthcare and DCC Technology businesses as part of the Group's strategic refocusing on energy.
evidence.quote: As of 31 March 2026, our total number of Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) stood at 11,700 representing a decrease on the prior year’s total of 16,777. This reduction is largely due to the divestments of DCC Healthcare and DCC Technology businesses.

evidence.title: Disposal of DCC Technology's Info Tech business
evidence.summary: DCC Technology completed the sale of its Info Tech businesses in November 2025, materially reducing complexity and working capital volatility. The remaining Technology operations are targeted for sale during calendar year 2026.
evidence.quote: Within DCC Technology, the sale of our Info Tech businesses completed in November 2025, materially reducing complexity and working capital volatility... Our objective is to agree a sale of the remaining Technology operations during the calendar year 2026, subject to market conditions and achieving appropriate value.

evidence.title: Sale of DCC Healthcare
evidence.summary: DCC completed the sale of DCC Healthcare, announced in April 2025, as a major milestone in delivering the strategy announced in November 2024 to focus on energy. This divestment materially reduced complexity and enabled capital return to shareholders.
evidence.quote: The sale of DCC Healthcare, which was announced in April 2025, was a major milestone in delivering the strategy announced in November 2024.

evidence.title: DCC becoming a focused energy business, renaming to DCC Energy
evidence.summary: DCC is simplifying its portfolio to focus solely on energy, divesting Healthcare and Technology businesses, and will change its name to DCC Energy plc. This represents a fundamental business model shift from a diversified conglomerate to a single-sector energy company.
evidence.quote: We are simplifying DCC to focus on energy, our largest growth and returns opportunity. This year DCC plc will become DCC Energy plc.

initiatives.name: European Liquid Gas Expansion
initiatives.summary: DCC committed approximately £110 million (£112.4 million per KPI disclosure) to acquisitions, mainly in European liquid gas markets, strengthening positions in resilient cash-generating markets with decarbonisation pathways and expanding into Central Europe.

evidence.title: ~£110-112.4 million committed acquisition expenditure, mainly European liquid gas
evidence.summary: DCC committed approximately £110 million (£112.4 million per KPI disclosure) to acquisitions, mainly in European liquid gas markets, strengthening positions in resilient cash-generating markets with decarbonisation pathways and expanding into Central Europe.
evidence.quote: we committed approximately £110 million to acquisitions mainly in European liquid gas markets... Committed acquisitions since the prior year Results Announcement amounted to £112.4 million.

evidence.title: €UGI International Central European liquid gas acquisitions
evidence.summary: DCC Energy agreed in January 2026 to acquire UGI International's liquid gas businesses in Poland, Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia, marking entry into four new Central European markets, supplying over 200 million litres annually to ~30,000 customers.
evidence.quote: In January 2026, DCC announced an agreement to acquire UGI International’s liquid gas businesses in Poland, Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia, marking entry into four new Central European markets in a single, highly complementary transaction.

evidence.title: FLAGA and AvantiGas liquid gas acquisitions
evidence.summary: DCC Energy completed the acquisition of FLAGA GmbH, a leading Austrian liquid gas distributor (entering the Austrian market, ~45 million litres/year, 15,000+ customers), and the AvantiGas cylinder business in the UK, strengthening its leadership position there.
evidence.quote: DCC acquired FLAGA GmbH, a leading Austrian liquid gas distributor, marking entry into the Austrian market with a well-invested business supplying approximately 45 million litres annually to more than 15,000 customers. In parallel, DCC completed the acquisition of the AvantiGas cylinder business in the UK.

initiatives.name: Global Learning Management System Rollout
initiatives.summary: DCC rolled out a new global Learning Management System to over 1,200 DCC Energy colleagues across the UK, Ireland, Sweden and Denmark, providing a consistent platform for learning, development and compliance training, with 19% increase in users.

evidence.title: Global Learning Management System rollout
evidence.summary: DCC rolled out a new global Learning Management System to over 1,200 DCC Energy colleagues across the UK, Ireland, Sweden and Denmark, providing a consistent platform for learning, development and compliance training, with 19% increase in users.
evidence.quote: This year, we rolled out a global Learning Management System to over 1,200 DCC Energy colleagues across the UK, Ireland, Sweden and Denmark, providing a consistent platform for learning, development and compliance training.

evidence.title: Learning content provider partnership for employee development
evidence.summary: DCC partnered with a leading learning content provider to give employees access to e-learning content, live learning sessions, and scenario-based AI simulations to support professional development.
evidence.quote: To provide our people with access to high-quality learning, in the financial year that ended 31 March 2026 we partnered with a leading learning content provider. Through this partnership, colleagues with access to our learning platform can now engage with a wide range of resources, including e-learning content, live learning sessions, and scenario-based AI simulations.

initiatives.name: Scope 3 Emissions Reduction Target
initiatives.summary: DCC targets a 35% reduction in Scope 3 GHG emissions by 2030 against a 2022 baseline, having achieved a 14% cumulative reduction to date, driven by increased biofuel sales and lower fuel volumes.

evidence.title: Scope 3 emissions reduction target of 35% by 2030
evidence.summary: DCC targets a 35% reduction in Scope 3 GHG emissions by 2030 against a 2022 baseline, having achieved a 14% cumulative reduction to date, driven by increased biofuel sales and lower fuel volumes.
evidence.quote: We have a target to reduce Scope 3 emissions by 35% by 2030 against a 2022 baseline and have achieved a 14% reduction to date.

initiatives.name: Scope 1 & 2 Emissions Reduction Target
initiatives.summary: DCC has a target to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% by 2030 against a 2019 baseline, having achieved a 45% reduction to date, partly driven by divestment of Healthcare and Technology businesses.

evidence.title: Scope 1 & 2 emissions reduction target of 50% by 2030
evidence.summary: DCC has a target to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% by 2030 against a 2019 baseline, having achieved a 45% reduction to date, partly driven by divestment of Healthcare and Technology businesses.
evidence.quote: We have to date achieved a 45% reduction against our target of a 50% reduction by 2030.

initiatives.name: Asia-Pacific Liquid Gas Divestment
initiatives.summary: DCC disposed of its Hong Kong & Macau liquid gas business in July 2024 as part of ongoing portfolio changes, contributing to softer first-half comparatives in the following year.

evidence.title: DCC Healthcare / Hong Kong & Macau liquid gas disposal
evidence.summary: DCC disposed of its Hong Kong & Macau liquid gas business in July 2024 as part of ongoing portfolio changes, contributing to softer first-half comparatives in the following year.
evidence.quote: A softer first half reflected strong prior year comparatives, weather effects and portfolio changes, including the disposal of our Hong Kong & Macau liquid gas business in July 2024.

initiatives.name: Board Composition Refresh
initiatives.summary: John Abbott will join the DCC Board in July 2026, bringing global energy sector experience to strengthen the Board's capability in overseeing the energy strategy and transition-related risks.

evidence.title: Board retirements: Mark Ryan and Laura Angelini
evidence.summary: Mark Ryan will retire from the Board at the conclusion of the AGM on 16 July 2026, with Steven Holland appointed as Workforce Engagement Director. Laura Angelini also announced her intention to retire from the Board at the same AGM.
evidence.quote: We previously announced that Mark Ryan will retire from the Board at the conclusion of our AGM on 16 July 2026. The Board was very pleased to appoint Steven Holland to take on the role of Workforce Engagement Director when Mark retires. More recently, Laura Angelini indicated her intention to retire from the Board at the conclusion of our AGM this year.

evidence.title: John Abbott appointed to the Board
evidence.summary: John Abbott will join the DCC Board in July 2026, bringing global energy sector experience to strengthen the Board's capability in overseeing the energy strategy and transition-related risks.
evidence.quote: I am pleased that John Abbott will join the Board in July 2026, bringing deep and highly relevant global energy sector experience.

initiatives.name: EV Charging Infrastructure Investment
initiatives.summary: DCC invested £168.1 million in net capital expenditure for the year, primarily in tanks, cylinders and installations for liquid gas customers, plus investment in Mobility service stations including EV fast charging infrastructure and digital enhancements in Technology.

evidence.title: £168.1 million net capital expenditure including EV charging infrastructure
evidence.summary: DCC invested £168.1 million in net capital expenditure for the year, primarily in tanks, cylinders and installations for liquid gas customers, plus investment in Mobility service stations including EV fast charging infrastructure and digital enhancements in Technology.
evidence.quote: Net capital expenditure amounted to £168.1 million for the year (2025: £169.1 million)... In Mobility, capital investment was focused on maintaining and optimising the service station network and upgrading capabilities across the business, including the addition of electric vehicle fast charging infrastructure and enhanced forecourt services.

initiatives.name: Shareholder Capital Return Programme
initiatives.summary: Following the Healthcare sale, the Board approved returning £700 million to shareholders through a £100 million on-market share buyback and a £600 million tender offer, reflecting disciplined capital allocation after portfolio simplification.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £700 million (£100 million buyback + £600 million tender offer)

evidence.title: £700 million capital return via buyback and tender offer

evidence.quote: approved the return of £700 million to shareholders through a £100 million on market share buyback and a £600 million tender offer.

initiatives.name: HVO Feedstock Sourcing & Fraud Prevention
initiatives.summary: DCC undertook a review of Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (HVO) sourcing and feedstock assurance to enhance transparency given market concerns about feedstock fraud and limitations in the ISCC certification system.

evidence.title: HVO feedstock sourcing and fraud-prevention review
evidence.summary: DCC undertook a review of Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (HVO) sourcing and feedstock assurance to enhance transparency given market concerns about feedstock fraud and limitations in the ISCC certification system.
evidence.quote: We have undertaken a review of Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (‘HVO’) sourcing and feedstock assurance. There is a need for enhanced transparency, particularly given concerns raised in the market regarding feedstock fraud and limitations in the International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (‘ISCC’) system.
